records.name: Autophagy
records.tldr: Autophagy delivers cellular material for breakdown and reuse. The amount present, the rate of recycling and whether cells need it to survive are different questions.
records.summary: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in autophagosomes for lysosomal delivery and breakdown. LC3 abundance alone cannot distinguish increased formation from reduced removal. Tandem fluorescent LC3 reporters exploit different responses to acidic and degradative conditions to examine maturation in cell experiments; interpretation requires appropriate controls. Flux and survival dependence need separate tests. In a randomised phase 2 trial of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. A drug trial does not by itself establish selective autophagy dependence in a tumour.

Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

Product return has evidence in defined systems. In leucine-starved cultured human HEK-293T cells, Wyant and colleagues found that SLC38A9 was needed for leucine made by lysosomal protein breakdown to reach the cytosol; the response also depended on the autophagy protein ATG7. Abu-Remaileh and colleagues measured regulated lysosomal amino-acid exchange in mammalian cells. Yeast experiments identified Atg22, Avt3 and Avt4 as partially redundant vacuolar amino-acid exporters. These results support amino-acid recycling in those systems, without establishing transport of every breakdown product, secretion from the cell or guaranteed growth.

More lipidated LC3-II can reflect greater formation or slower removal. A controlled short lysosomal block and complementary tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter can help examine turnover and delivery to acidic compartments. Equal starting amounts can have different later fates. Little additional accumulation can reflect a late block, low formation or an unsuitable window; it does not establish dependence.

Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. Use time courses, viable-cell normalisation, verified lysosomal inhibition and independent perturbations; autophagy proteins can have other functions. Lower mTOR signalling can change initiation without guaranteeing completed degradation. Typical research outputs include normalised LC3-II band intensity, reporter compartments per cell and selected-cargo disappearance over time. Tested cultures are consumed or perturbed, and prolonged lysosomal inhibition can itself disturb the system. No universal LC3 or flux cutoff selects treatment.

In Karasic and colleagues' randomised phase 2 study of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel increased response rate but did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. Response was 38.2% versus 21.1%; 12-month survival was 41% versus 49%. These group results do not show selective autophagy dependence or recommend this combination.

Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.

Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and the RB1CC1-encoded protein FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.
records.analogy: A besieged city that starts recycling furniture into firewood. It keeps the lights on through the siege, and burning the 'wanted posters' (MHC) hides its criminals too.
interventions: Clinical drug studies and mechanistic dependence tests answer different questions.
Assess flux, selected cargo and survival separately with complementary controls.

records.name: BRD4
aka: BET bromodomain proteins (BRD2, BRD3, BRD4, BRDT)
records.tldr: BRD4 reads acetyl marks on DNA-packaging proteins and helps regulate transcription. Blocking a recognition pocket and removing the whole protein test different functions.
records.summary:
BRD4 is a chromatin reader that recognizes acetylated histones and helps regulate transcription. Its recognition pockets and other protein interactions can contribute different functions.

Engaging an acetyl-recognition pocket and depleting a whole protein are different interventions. In selected TNBC models with acquired BET-inhibitor resistance, cells remained dependent on BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. Verify pocket engagement and depletion independently before comparing growth outcomes. Neither operation alone establishes clinical benefit or a vulnerability caused by an uncharacterized BET-family variant.

BET proteins read acetylated lysine marks; they do not write the acetyl mark. The family includes BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 and BRDT, with two bromodomains and an extra-terminal interaction region. BRD4 can recruit transcription-elongation machinery, but other bromodomain proteins are not all BET proteins and family members are not functionally interchangeable. A schematic that retains the same histone mark during pocket occupation and protein depletion isolates two different interventions. The fixed mark is a drawing convention rather than a measured unchanged acetylation state; the state of the mark needs its own measurement. A representative pocket also does not make JQ1 specific to BD1.

In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. The findings can coexist if the remaining protein supplies functions the probe does not block, as the resistant-model work illustrates. Binding assays, chromatin occupancy, early RNA changes, later growth and death, general transcription effects and appropriate restoration controls answer different questions. Lower MYC RNA alone does not attribute a later effect to MYC.

French identified a BRD4-NUT fusion in the defined carcinoma; a fusion is a different biological alteration from an ordinary sequence variant. Stathis reported four people with confirmed BRD4-NUT carcinomas treated with OTX015/MK-8628 in compassionate use: two had rapid regression, with no randomized comparison or established survival benefit. The report described thrombocytopenia, including reversible grade 3 events and a grade 4 event in one patient. This small selected series does not establish efficacy across BET-altered tumors.

BET proteins contain two recognition domains, BD1 and BD2, alongside other interaction regions. JQ1 competes with acetylated binding partners at these pockets. It was developed as an experimental chemical probe, with binding measured across bromodomains. The original work found binding to both BRD4 bromodomains and other BET-family members; a drawing of one occupied pocket does not make the compound specific to BD1. Compare the actual protein and domain profile of each compound. A preference for BD2, or for one family member, is not comparative evidence of human safety or anticancer benefit. Pocket occupation also leaves protein regions that a separately verified depletion experiment removes.

Piha-Paul and colleagues reported a first-in-human molibresib study in NUT carcinoma and other solid tumours, published online in 2019 and in the 2020 journal issue. The dose-escalation report included 65 patients and assessed exposure, pharmacodynamic effects, safety and preliminary activity. Thrombocytopenia and gastrointestinal events were frequent treatment-related adverse events in this study. Circulating monocyte chemoattractant protein 1 was a pharmacodynamic measurement, not a patient-benefit endpoint. These findings describe this product and study; they do not rank every BET inhibitor or show postoperative benefit in triple-negative breast cancer.

A binding or displacement assay tests the pocket interaction; chromatin occupancy and RNA output test later biological effects. Cell counts, growth, death and regrowth after washout answer further questions. State the protein or domain tested, compound, concentration, duration and comparator. Nanomolar, abbreviated nM, means one billionth of a mole per litre; RNA counts and signals normalised to a control use their own units. Genetic perturbation, an independent compound, comparison cells and monitoring of general transcription help distinguish a specific dependence from broad disruption. No single one of these readouts is a clinical sensitivity score.

Consider a fictional culture in which a BET inhibitor lowers MYC RNA while cells continue growing. The RNA change shows a measured transcriptional effect, not MYC-mediated cell death or absence of every remaining BET function. Check which protein and pocket were engaged, the timing of the RNA and growth measurements, general transcription, independently controlled protein perturbation and comparison cells. Shu and colleagues found that selected inhibitor-resistant triple-negative breast-cancer cultures still required BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. That result explains why pocket response and whole-protein dependence can diverge; it does not predict patient benefit from the fictional result.

A BRD3 sequence variant, BRD4 dependence and sensitivity to a compound acting across BET proteins are three separate propositions. A family name cannot connect them without functional evidence. To explain a BET result, identify the reading interaction being perturbed, show which protein functions account for the measured effect and then state the comparative clinical evidence. Decreased MYC RNA is also different from directly inhibiting MYC protein.

records.name: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
records.tldr: Cell-free DNA is DNA outside intact cells in a collected sample. Tumour-derived DNA is one possible part of that mixture; its amount depends on the specimen and method.
records.summary:
Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is DNA outside intact cells in a specimen. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is the tumour-derived part of the plasma DNA mixture, rather than a different material competing with cfDNA. DNA from non-tumour tissues can contribute much of that mixture, as illustrated by Moss and colleagues' methylation-atlas study. Total extracted DNA is therefore not a tumour measurement. A finite evaluated aliquot can contain no qualifying tumour signal even when disease exists elsewhere.

Liquid biopsy describes a specimen approach. A test may track known tumour features, look for predefined mutation, methylation or fragment patterns, or profile detectable alterations. Its target coverage, origin checks, sample requirements and calling rule determine the claim. Genotyping, residual-disease monitoring and screening have different intended uses; a method label does not validate every use or locate the source of a plasma signal.

notes: Source classes: cfDNA is DNA outside intact cells in a sample, and ctDNA is the tumour-derived part of that pool, so the two are related materials and not rival tests. In healthy donors a methylation atlas of 25 tissues and cell types attributed plasma cfDNA to white blood cells (55%), erythrocyte progenitors (30%), vascular endothelial cells (10%) and hepatocytes (1%) (Moss 2018). A tumour adds DNA only when it contributes, and the tumour share may be small or absent in the sample drawn even when cancer exists elsewhere.

Scale: plasma DNA fragments show a pattern reminiscent of nuclease-cleaved nucleosomes with a peak at 166 base pairs (Lo 2010, in maternal plasma), and tumour-derived fragments are enriched at 90 to 150 base pairs (Mouliere 2018). One assay input in a breast-cancer comparison was 4,500 amplifiable copies, about 15 nanograms (Santonja 2023), and at about 3.3 picograms per haploid genome copy 1 nanogram is roughly 300 copies (arithmetic from genome size). In a fictional single-locus model with 4,500 amplifiable opportunities and target-allele probability 1 in 100,000, the expected target count is 0.045. The target-allele probability is not automatically a tumour-DNA fraction: copy number, variant multiplicity and clone representation matter.

Yield is not origin: in a fictional experiment equal 1 mL plasma aliquots give 2 and 4 nanograms of cfDNA and no tumour-attributed signal is reported. Total DNA doubled, but tumour fraction and any tumour-DNA fold change cannot be calculated because tumour attribution was not measured. A fragment's source needs evidence such as paired white-blood-cell and tumour sequencing (Razavi 2019), and a variant seen in plasma is not automatically tumour-derived.

Method card: measures selected features of plasma DNA by a stated sequencing or molecular method, from a finite plasma aliquot that testing consumes. Output is detected or not detected, variant fractions, molecule concentrations or model estimates, each with its own unit. It cannot give an all-body cell count, lesion location, viability or treatment benefit, and validity belongs to the exact specimen, assay version and intended use.

Collection conditions can change the mixture before testing: blood-cell breakdown adds genomic DNA and can dilute a tumour fraction. The NCI biospecimen practices document, revised February 2025, prefers plasma to serum. Its protocol recommends EDTA, accepts acid citrate dextrose, and advises avoiding heparin and citrate; the literature-summary section separately reports results with several anticoagulants when processing was immediate. For EDTA blood the protocol prefers centrifugation within 2 hours and accepts up to 4 hours at room temperature or 24 hours at 4 degrees Celsius; it recommends stabilising tubes for anticipated delays over 2 hours. These are recommendations for that specimen workflow, not a universal acceptance rule for every assay. Extraction and library preparation then retain only some available molecules, so the volume drawn is not the volume evaluated.

Reading an assay report starts with the specimen and collection date, the plasma volume actually evaluated, DNA quality and recovery, origin checks, and the rule that turns a signal into a call. Low shedding, damaged input or failed quality controls can limit interpretation; a failed assay is a separate result from no qualifying signal. Genotyping, response monitoring and residual-disease detection are different intended uses. In its November 2024 drug-development guidance, FDA asks for validation of the complete workflow, representative clinical samples, the input range and prespecified calling cut-offs; validation of one use does not establish another.

A useful result ledger keeps six questions together: when the sample was collected and where that date sits relative to treatment or surgery; the assay and version; the specimen, evaluated input and quality qualifications; the reported state, including detected, not detected, indeterminate or failed; the quantity, unit and numerical qualifications; and the applicable detection and quantitation criteria. Keep the report-release date separately. Two reports arriving together may describe different biological moments, and an invalid sample or failed reference build is not a negative plasma result.

In a fictional comparison, one assay reports not detected and another reports a low detected signal. That alone does not identify an erroneous test. Compare the actual samples and collection dates, targets, input, controls and calling criteria before interpreting the disagreement. A valid negative says that the evaluated sample did not meet that method's qualifying-signal rule. It cannot distinguish every possibility: there may be no residual tumour signal, too few relevant fragments may have reached the aliquot, or the tracked features may not represent the remaining cells. This reading exercise sets no repeat-draw schedule.

records.name: Chemical probe
records.tldr: A chemical probe is a compound used in the laboratory to switch one biological process off or on and ask what it does, so it is judged by how well it is characterised for that question and not by whether it could be given to a person.
records.summary:
A chemical probe is a research compound used to perturb a defined biological process in cells or animals. It is useful only to the extent that it is potent enough, selective enough and characterised well enough for the question being asked. Arrowsmith and colleagues put the requirement as a probe that is potent, of known selectivity and with a proven mechanism of action, and describe how many probes in common use were first characterised inadequately and later proved to be nonselective. LY294002 was described in 1994 as a selective inhibitor of PI3 kinase and was still sold as one by nearly all vendors, although by 2005 it was clear that it inhibited many other proteins at the concentrations used to inhibit PI3 kinase. An effect seen in cells at a high concentration therefore identifies an effect at that concentration, not necessarily a target.

The numerical standards belong to the groups that set them. For probes of epigenetic targets, the Structural Genomics Consortium as described by Arrowsmith and colleagues asks minimally for in vitro potency at the target below 100 nM, more than 30-fold selectivity over related proteins of the same family, profiling against a standard panel of off-targets and effects on the target in cells below 1 uM, and now requires an inactive close analogue as a negative control. Workman and Collins advocate assessing fitness for the intended experiment rather than applying an overly restrictive universal rule. Those cut-offs were written for particular target classes and do not apply to every probe, and neither paper offers a number that makes a concentration universally clean.

Controls carry the causal argument. An inactive or weakly active analogue from the same chemical family asks whether the effect follows the target-binding feature rather than shared chemistry; an active probe of a different chemical structure asks whether an independent perturbation agrees, with the limit that two probes can still share an off-target; and a genetic change or engineered resistance asks whether altering the target alters the effect as predicted, with the limit that removing a whole protein is different from blocking one of its functions. Workman and Collins add that a chemical probe can inhibit a specific function rather than remove the protein, which RNA interference cannot, and that both approaches have off-target as well as on-target effects. Agreement among these tests strengthens an inference, and conflicts should be recorded rather than set aside.

A probe is not a medicine. Arrowsmith and colleagues note that a probe does not need to meet the requirements of a successful medicine, such as good pharmacodynamics and oral bioavailability, and that high-quality probes have served as seeds for new medicines. A medicine also needs evidence in people about product quality, exposure, tolerability and benefit for its intended use, so a useful probe may lack adequate delivery, stability or safety, and an approved medicine can be a poor tool for isolating one target if several of its interactions contribute to its effects; this is an evidence-reading distinction rather than a claim that the same experiment establishes clinical suitability. A culture concentration is not a patient dose.

Target engagement is the separate question of whether a compound interacts with its target where the experiment needs it. The cellular thermal shift assay, introduced by Martinez Molina and colleagues, is built on ligand-induced thermal stabilisation of target proteins and was used to monitor drug binding in cells and tissue samples; a shift can support engagement under the assay conditions and is not by itself an inhibition or occupancy percentage. Engagement, a change in target function and cell survival are three measurements, and an effect on viability does not identify the responsible target.

Worked example, fictional. A new compound lowers the viability of cultured cells at 10 micromoles per litre, and neither engagement nor selectivity has been measured. The supported statement is that the compound has an effect in this culture at this concentration. It does not show that a particular protein is essential, and it does not show that a safe human dose reaches that protein. To close those gaps one would measure engagement and relevant selectivity, test an inactive analogue and a chemically different probe, and perturb the target genetically or by engineered resistance. Those steps address causality; exposure, quality, safety and clinical evidence remain separate questions.

notes: Record the chemical identity, structure, source and purity, concentration-dependent activity, selectivity and effects in the relevant system. An inactive close analogue is useful, but its uptake or other properties may differ; an unrelated active probe can still share an off-target. Removing a whole protein can differ from inhibiting one function. Agreement among controls strengthens an inference in that system, and disagreement belongs in the evidence record rather than being discarded.

records.name: Controlled perturbation experiment
records.tldr: Controlled perturbations deliberately change specified factors and compare responses with suitable controls. A model response alone does not prove its mechanism or patient benefit.
records.summary: A controlled perturbation deliberately changes a defined factor and measures the response against appropriate comparison conditions. Vehicle, positive, negative and mechanism controls answer different questions. A reproducible response can support an experimental claim without establishing its proposed mechanism or patient benefit. Baseline growth, timing, dose and the actual unit assigned to treatment matter.

notes: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

records.name: ctDNA units, fractions and concentrations
records.tldr: A ctDNA result is a number with a unit. Molecules per millilitre, parts per million and allele fraction answer different questions, so a printed number means nothing until its unit and denominator are known.
records.summary:
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) can be reported as a concentration, as a fraction, or as a yes or no call, and the three are not interchangeable. A concentration counts tumour-attributed molecules in a stated volume of plasma. One example is mean tumour molecules per millilitre (MTM/mL), which the I-SPY 2 breast-cancer study of Magbanua and colleagues used for ctDNA across tracked variants. A fraction divides tumour-attributed molecules by a stated total, such as all evaluated alleles at one position (variant allele fraction, VAF) or all evaluated DNA (an estimated tumour fraction). Parts per million (PPM) is a fraction multiplied by one million, so the number is only as meaningful as the fraction it scales: 0.01% is 100 PPM, and 0.00024% is 2.4 PPM, the lowest allele fraction Santonja and colleagues reported for ctDNA detection in breast cancer.

Concentration and fraction can move apart. If two equal one-millilitre aliquots each hold the same number of tumour molecules but one holds more background cell-free DNA, the concentration is unchanged and the fraction falls. A detection call and a reliable amount are also different claims, because the detection limit and the quantitation range are validated separately. Nothing here gives a conversion between assays: MTM/mL cannot be turned into PPM from the printed result, and a VAF of 100 PPM at one variant is not a tumour fraction of 100 PPM.

notes: Method card, what it measures: the quantity an assay states, either a count of tumour-attributed molecules per volume of plasma (a concentration), a share of a named total (a fraction), or a call. How: sequencing or PCR on one finite plasma aliquot, then a calculation the laboratory defines. Keep the unit, the denominator and the assay version attached to every value.

Table, MTM/mL: mean tumour molecules per millilitre of plasma under the assay's own calculation across its tracked features. Boundary: a concentration estimated from tracked features, not the number of cancer cells per millilitre and not a share of anything.

Table, PPM: parts per million, a fraction multiplied by one million, so 1 PPM is 0.0001% and 100 PPM is 0.01%. Boundary: name the fraction being scaled, because 100 PPM of variant alleles, of evaluated DNA and of tumour-attributed molecules are three different claims.

Table, variant allele fraction: the share of evaluated alleles at one position that carry a stated variant. Boundary: it depends on copy number, on which clones carry the variant and on the measurement, and a variant present in a blood-cell clone counts the same way as one from a tumour.

Table, tumour fraction: an estimated share of evaluated DNA attributable to tumour. Boundary: it is a model output that rests on the method and its calibration, and it is not automatically any single variant's VAF.

Fictional arithmetic, concentration against fraction: two equal 1 mL aliquots each hold 4 tumour-attributed molecules. Aliquot A also holds 16 background molecules, so 4 of 20 is 20% and the concentration is 4 molecules per mL. Aliquot B holds 36 background molecules, so 4 of 40 is 10% and the concentration is still 4 per mL. More background lowered the fraction and left the concentration alone. These toy shares are not a VAF, an estimated tumour fraction or MTM/mL.

Fictional arithmetic, rescaling: a VAF of 0.01% at Variant R equals 100 PPM of variant-supporting alleles. That does not make a tumour fraction of 100 PPM, and a second report of 0.2 MTM/mL is a concentration, so 100 and 0.2 cannot be compared or converted without the methods and calibration of both assays.

Method limit, detection against quantitation: a qualifying detection call and a reliable numerical amount have separate validation criteria. A detected value below the validated quantitative range does not support an exact fold change, and extra decimal places do not create precision.

Method limit, finite input: the plasma volume drawn is not the volume or the number of molecules recovered and evaluated. Low molecular counts, changes in background DNA, poor recovery or incompatible calibration all limit comparison across assays, and a printed zero is not a count of zero cancer cells anywhere in the body.

Evidence read: in Magbanua's 84-patient pilot of neoadjuvant treatment, ctDNA in MTM/mL was correlated with MRI functional tumour volume at every time point (Spearman rho 0.42 to 0.49). Santonja's comparison reported allele fractions down to 2.4 PPM for hybrid-capture sequencing of 1,347 to 7,491 tumour-identified mutations and 4.7 PPM for multiplex PCR of 21 to 47 structural variants. Each figure belongs to its assay and cohort.

A trend also needs the collection time, treatment context, assay version and quantitative range. In its November 2024 drug-development guidance, FDA asks for precision, accuracy and detection-limit evaluation across relevant inputs and cut-offs, using representative clinical specimens and appropriately comparable reference material. A printed number below another assay's nominal detection limit does not establish that the other assay would miss that sample: the measured quantity, specimen, input, recovery and calling rules may differ. A reference-material result is not automatically a clinical sensitivity estimate.

Consider a fictional assay estimating tumour fraction at 6 parts per million (PPM) and then 2 PPM. Both samples are called detected, but the second is below the assay's reliable quantitation range. The printed estimates fall by two-thirds; they do not establish that the cancer volume fell by two-thirds. Retain the qualifying calls and uncertainty, because shedding and background DNA can change the signal. A second method reporting molecules per millilitre cannot simply be placed on this fraction scale. Even a matching unit label does not establish matching calibration. Keeping serial methods and input comparable helps interpretation without removing biological variation.

The blank, detection and quantitation limits answer different questions. The blank limit is the highest apparent analyte concentration expected from replicate samples with no analyte; the detection limit is the lowest concentration reliably distinguished from that background; the quantitation limit is the lowest concentration meeting predefined bias and imprecision goals (Armbruster and Pry, 2008). Quantitation and detection limits may coincide or differ. A qualifying detection below a validated quantitative range supports presence more strongly than an exact fold change. For a read-based variant allele fraction, the denominator is informative reads covering that locus, not cancer cells or plasma volume; keep a molecule-based method's own definition instead.

records.name: Endoplasmic reticulum stress and the unfolded protein response
records.tldr: Cells respond to strain on protein folding through several signalling branches. A response does not by itself establish cell death.
records.summary: The unfolded protein response has distinct outputs. IRE1-dependent processing of XBP1 RNA produces a potent transcriptional regulator; total XBP1 message and its spliced fraction are different measurements. PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and can reduce translation initiation. ER stress also promotes ATF6 proteolysis, releasing a fragment that acts in the nucleus. These findings come from molecular and cell experiments. Branch activity, adaptation, survival dependence and treatment benefit require separate evidence. Specify branch, timing, total protein or RNA controls and direct growth and death measurements.

IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.

ATF6 travels from ER to Golgi for processing; the released fragment, rather than the intact membrane-bound precursor, acts in the nucleus. Total XBP1 RNA differs from its splice-form fraction. Other kinases can phosphorylate eIF2alpha, so one phosphosite cannot identify the whole response.

Splice-form fractions, processed ATF6 and defined phosphoprotein signals are different outputs. Increased XBP1 splicing with stable viable-cell counts supports a branch response, not lethal stress; measure growth and death directly and test causality independently. RNA or protein preparations and compatible tissue stains use material; functional dependence tests require viable cells. XBP1 depletion altered tumour growth and relapse in defined triple-negative breast cancer models, with an HIF1alpha transcriptional interaction. Model findings and patient expression-signature associations do not establish universal XBP1 dependence, an assay cutoff or a treatment benefit. Successful stress adaptation can support survival.

records.name: Ferroptosis & regulated cell death
records.tldr: Ferroptosis is a form of cell death involving iron-dependent membrane-lipid damage. General oxidative stress or one positive marker does not establish this mechanism.
records.summary: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation and death. Cystine uptake through system xc- can support cysteine and glutathione availability; it does not transport glutathione itself. GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides, while FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q-associated defence. Dependence on these routes varies with the model and cellular conditions. Establishing the mechanism requires appropriately controlled measurements of death, lipid damage, iron dependence and rescue, with complementary perturbations. Findings in persistent or mesenchymal model cells do not establish a universal vulnerability or a treatment recommendation. Necrotic appearance, danger signals and adaptive antitumour immunity are separate questions.

Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation causing death. Erastin experiments implicated cystine uptake through system xc-, connecting cysteine and glutathione supply to antioxidant defence. Vulnerable polyunsaturated lipid chains, iron availability and cellular conditions matter; general reactive-oxygen fluorescence does not establish this mechanism.

GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides to lipid alcohols. FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q radical-trapping defence; it does not replace every GPX4 function or describe the whole protection network. Protein abundance alone does not measure protective activity or predict compound sensitivity.

Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. Probe chemistry, concentration, nutrients, cell density and observation time can alter results. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

A culture with abundant GPX4, a general oxidation signal and no death has not demonstrated ferroptosis. Cell-line and xenograft vulnerabilities do not establish tolerable exposure, selective cancer killing or benefit in patients. Alternative defences can confer resistance, so a strong antioxidant programme is not automatically a treatment vulnerability.

Hangauer 2017 investigated reversible drug-tolerant persister states across specified cancer-cell and drug models. Surviving the original treatment could coexist with increased GPX4 dependence; this was not necessarily permanent genetic resistance. The breast model BT474 is HER2-positive, not a triple-negative model. In the mouse relapse experiment, A375 melanoma cells had genetic GPX4 loss, with ferrostatin protection withdrawn while dabrafenib and trametinib continued. Prevented relapse in that setting was not systemic treatment with a GPX4 inhibitor: the authors noted poor systemic pharmacokinetics of RSL3 and ML210. These experiments do not establish a tolerable human window or universal persister vulnerability.

A fictional GPX4 experiment combines lipid oxidation before death, rescue by an iron chelator and a lipid-radical trap, and a corresponding phenotype after an independent genetic perturbation. These observations converge on an iron-dependent lipid-damage explanation; none alone proves it. Include vehicle, rescue-only and an unrelated death condition because rescue compounds can affect other processes. Survival of an otherwise matched FSP1-high comparison is compatible with a parallel defence; directly testing that defence is needed before assigning compensation to it. Energy production, a general oxidation dye and an antioxidant transcript are different measurements and cannot substitute for this causal sequence.
records.analogy: Ferroptosis is rust. Iron plus oxygen eats through the cell's membranes unless an antioxidant crew (GPX4) keeps repainting them. Cells that changed shape to dodge chemotherapy have thinner paint.

Pattern or module score, subtype classifier and outcome predictor answer different questions; performance belongs to a population, endpoint and horizon.

Analytical repeatability, clinical validity and clinical utility are separate questions.
A bulk inflammatory signature can rise from more immune cells, changed state or both; a stress score does not establish protein activation, metabolic rate or dependence.

An expression score requires compatible RNA input, locked preprocessing, genes, weights, reference, endpoint/horizon and software version. Existing data can be rescored without new tissue; acquiring RNA consumes material. Report categories, ranks, probabilities or unitless scores on their exact scale. Missing genes, batch, mixture and population shift undermine cutoffs; analytical, clinical and utility evidence remain separate.

An expression-program score has meaning within its algorithm and background. For a score formed by subtracting matched control-gene expression, zero need not mean that no program genes were detected. The 90th percentile places a result relative to a specified reference; it does not mean that 90 percent of cells express the program or that a pathway is 90 percent active. Changing the genes, preprocessing, controls or reference can change the scale, so retain them with the method and version.

records.name: KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway
records.tldr: KEAP1-NRF2 regulates cellular stress defences. Protection, metabolic dependence and treatment response need separate tests in the relevant cancer and conditions.
records.summary:
KEAP1 helps a CUL3-containing ubiquitin-ligase system regulate NRF2 turnover. Loss of relevant KEAP1 function can stabilise NRF2 and increase antioxidant, detoxification and drug-export programmes. A gene alteration or high RNA signal alone does not establish its functional direction, the affected cells or a treatment response.

Singh 2006 identified KEAP1 mutations in ten of 54 non-small-cell lung cancer samples, including primary tumours and pleural fluid. Among six mutation-bearing primary tumours assessed for the remaining locus, five had loss of heterozygosity. The cell experiments supported increased NRF2-related activity and drug-resistance mechanisms in those systems, rather than resistance to every therapy.

Romero 2017 used gene editing and metabolic experiments in KRAS-driven lung cancer models: Keap1 loss promoted tumour growth and created a glutaminolysis vulnerability in the tested systems. A protective programme can therefore coexist with a dependence on a different supply route. The randomised phase 2 KEAPSAKE registry records 40 actual participants and termination for lack of clinical benefit from the telaglenastat combination strategy. A preclinical dependence is not an approved treatment or a universal predictor of benefit.

Singh's initial series contained 40 primary lung cancers and 16 pleural-fluid samples; excluding two small-cell pleural-fluid samples gives the 54 NSCLC denominator. Ten mutation-bearing samples round to 19 per cent, not a universal lung-cancer prevalence. Five of six tested mutation-bearing primary tumours had locus loss; do not assign biallelic loss to all ten samples. Romero separately described KEAP1 alterations in about 20 per cent of KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinomas. These populations and denominators differ. KEAP1-mutant-versus-normal-cell viability comparisons are not matched isogenic proof that one alteration caused every chemotherapy response.

Protection and dependence are experiment-specific directions. If removing a verified defence makes a defined stress more lethal, that supports protection under that stress. If removing the defence or a supply route reduces survival relative to an appropriate matched comparison, that supports a conditional dependence; it need not mean every unstressed cell dies. In a fictional culture, high antioxidant RNA plus probe-associated death establishes neither NRF2-driven killing nor ferroptosis. Test the alteration's effect on NRF2 turnover or nuclear localisation and output, then use independent perturbation and restoration to examine the survival mechanism. CUL3 works with other adaptors, and a compound suppressing protein production broadly does not isolate NRF2. A genetic intervention also needs controls, rather than being automatically specific.

ClinicalTrials.gov records KEAPSAKE, NCT04265534, as a randomised, double-blind phase 2 comparison of telaglenastat or placebo added to carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab for selected metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC with KEAP1/NRF2 alterations. The record last updated in September 2022 reports actual enrollment 40, status terminated and the stated reason lack of clinical benefit. This is registry status, not a peer-reviewed effect estimate or proof that every glutaminase strategy fails. Model activity, eligibility, acceptable exposure and clinical benefit remain different questions.

Vartanian and colleagues examined brusatol in the KEAP1-mutant lung-cancer line A549. Protein profiling and measurements of newly synthesised proteins supported broad inhibition of protein synthesis, with NRF2 falling among many proteins. Cytotoxicity across additional cancer cell lines was not restricted to KEAP1-NRF2 activity. A lower NRF2 signal after this compound therefore does not isolate NRF2 inhibition as the cause of death. Check general translation early and use independently controlled perturbations before attributing a survival effect to the proposed defence.
records.analogy: A large fire service could reflect frequent fires, effective protection or dependence on a particular fuel supply. Counting equipment alone cannot distinguish those explanations; the corresponding cellular questions require activity, perturbation and survival measurements.
interventions: Investigate the exact alteration, NRF2 turnover or localisation and relevant target outputs before assigning pathway activity.
Test a proposed protective or metabolic dependence with defined perturbations, appropriate comparators and survival measurements.

records.name: Lipid synthesis, uptake & cholesterol
records.tldr: Cells can make, import, store and reuse lipids. The route they use and their dependence on it vary with the cell and conditions.
records.summary: Lipid metabolism includes synthesis, uptake, storage, membrane remodelling and oxidation. Cholesterol regulation and fatty-acid regulation overlap but are not interchangeable. Identify the SREBP member, cellular compartment and measured output rather than treating a transcript, precursor, nuclear fragment, sterol amount and synthesis rate as the same observation. SCAP-SREBP transport responds to endoplasmic reticulum cholesterol in the cited cell experiments. The mevalonate pathway supplies sterols and nonsterol products, including substrates for protein prenylation. Rescue by mevalonate therefore cannot uniquely identify cholesterol as the limiting product. Transcript abundance, lipid abundance, labelled production and a controlled survival-dependence experiment answer different questions. Results from a particular cell model or mouse experiment do not establish a universal tumour vulnerability or a preferred diet or treatment.

notes: SCAP and local endoplasmic-reticulum sterol conditions regulate transport of membrane-bound SREBP to the Golgi. Processing releases a fragment that enters the nucleus and regulates lipid synthesis and uptake. Sufficient local sterol supply can retain the complex in the ER; total cellular cholesterol and SREBP RNA do not measure this processing.

In the fictional supply experiment, nuclear SREBP-2 and uptake messages respond to lipid-poor medium; external lipid supply can reduce the response and compensate for synthesis perturbation. Record medium composition, density, timing and viability before assigning dependence. A supply-sensitive state does not establish the response of a person's tumour. Assess precursor and nuclear regulator, responsive transcripts, cellular sterols and uptake separately from labelled synthesis rates. Use controlled supplementation to test the proposed bottleneck; total amount does not specify production or local sensing. Lower synthesis does not itself show that a compound bound its target, and a medium effect does not identify uptake as its cause. An uncharacterised SCAP or MTOR variant needs evidence for its proposed functional effect; a gene name alone assigns neither activation nor loss of function.

In transgenic mice expressing a truncated SREBP-2 construct, Horton and colleagues observed preferential activation of cholesterol synthesis over fatty-acid synthesis in liver and adipose tissue, contrasting it with earlier SREBP-1a results. They separately measured transcripts and synthesis using labelled water. These are relative effects in a named experimental system, not exclusive duties of each family member or proof that a transcript measurement equals flux. Precursor location and nuclear processing require their own measurements.

Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and nonsterol products. In Freed-Pastor and colleagues' breast-cancer 3D cultures, geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate partially rescued an invasive phenotype after mutant-p53 depletion or simvastatin treatment. This illustrates why mevalonate rescue alone cannot uniquely attribute an effect to cholesterol. It does not identify every relevant metabolite, establish a universal cancer dependency or show that a statin perturbation reproduces every change in SCAP-SREBP regulation.

HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. Farnesyl and geranylgeranyl lipid modifications help position specified RAS- and RHO-family proteins, respectively. Cholesterol is a membrane component and a precursor of steroid hormones. Cholesterol amount, sterol synthesis and the whole mevalonate pathway are therefore different measurements. SCAP-SREBP sterol sensing regulates synthesis and uptake, but its activity, pathway transcripts, metabolite supply and dependence must each be established in the tested cells and medium.

Freed-Pastor 2012 studied mutant-p53 breast cancer cells in three-dimensional culture, with different outcomes in two triple-negative lines. Depleting mutant p53 reduced invasive behaviour in MDA-MB-231 but did not make it form ordered hollow acini; MDA-MB-468 could acquire a more ordered, hollow architecture. Statins reduced invasion in the former and caused growth inhibition with extensive death in the latter, rather than exactly reproducing every p53-depletion phenotype. Mutant-p53 depletion reduced mevalonate-pathway expression, and mevalonate add-back opposed several statin effects. This supports a pathway contribution in the studied systems without isolating cholesterol. The whole paper also examined growth, death and xenograft growth; it was not solely an architecture experiment, and none of these results established patient treatment benefit.

The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. Blocking the geranylgeranylation branch had a larger effect than the tested sterol-branch block, and GGPP partly restored invasive growth after mutant-p53 depletion or statin treatment. That is not evidence that GGPP rescues inhibition of the transferase itself, nor that every effect in both cell lines was entirely explained by one metabolite. The authors allowed contributions from other products. In a fictional supply comparison, synthesis falls under an inhibitor in both lipid-poor and lipid-rich medium, but growth slows mainly in the former while import is stipulated to compensate in the latter. Equal engagement with different growth outcomes is compatible with environmental supply; it is not a measurement of supply or dependence in a person's tumour.

records.name: MRD / molecular residual disease testing
records.tldr: Residual-disease testing looks for a qualifying disease signal after treatment in a specified sample. Some studies detect a signal before clinical recurrence, but the timing and detection rate depend on the assay and setting.
records.summary:
Residual-disease testing asks whether a qualifying disease signal is present after treatment in a specified sample. For solid tumours, plasma assays can look for selected tumour-associated DNA features, with results interpreted under their specimen, input, target and calling rules. Analytical detection, clinical detection in a population and recurrence association are different performance questions. A valid negative does not establish absence of every cancer cell.

Clinical usefulness belongs to a defined strategy: the cancer setting, assay, timing, triggering result, action and comparator. Evidence for genotyping, an approved indication or a strategy in another cancer does not automatically settle an early-breast-cancer question. The dated trial examples below retain their studied populations. More frequent detection, molecular clearance or favourable prognosis in treated negative groups does not by itself show improved patient outcomes or safe treatment omission.

notes: In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

A worked limit: for multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 patient-specific structural variants on 4,500 amplifiable copies, the theoretical limit is 1 / (4,500 x variants), which is 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million, at 47 variants. The 4.7 parts per million detection rested on a single mutant molecule, and one sample not detected at 4,500 copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies (Santonja 2023). Whole-genome sequencing of cfDNA integrates thousands of mutations and reached tumour-fraction sensitivity as low as 10 to the minus 5 (Zviran 2020).

What a lead-time figure here means: in García-Murillas 2019 ctDNA detection preceded clinical relapse by a median of 10.7 months in the combined cohort of 144, with the estimator and evaluable intervals needing distinction from the full cohort size. Distant extracranial relapse was detected in 22 of 23 patients and brain-only relapse in 1 of 6. Medians from different cohorts, schedules and confirmation rules cannot rank assays, and an earlier signal does not show that acting on it extends life.

Analytical detection and clinical sensitivity answer different questions. FDA diagnostic-test guidance dated March 2007 defines clinical sensitivity by the proportion testing positive among people who have the specified condition, judged against the reference standard in the intended-use population. In a residual-disease study, disease definition, follow-up, draw schedule, evaluable samples and recurrence sites shape that denominator. An analytical limit measured in prepared material does not supply that clinical proportion, and a negative test does not establish absence of cancer.

Clinical evidence belongs to a defined strategy. In the IMvigor011 randomised trial, 250 eligible patients with ctDNA-positive muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy received atezolizumab or placebo; disease-free and overall survival favoured atezolizumab (Powles 2025). This is evidence for that population and strategy, not for every positive residual-disease test, every cancer, or an arbitrary treatment change. Analytical detection, risk association, treatment-strategy benefit and a validated surrogate endpoint are different claims.

Read the evidence in stages. Analytical detection concerns the specified signal under stated test conditions, not detection in every person or draw. An association with recurrence is prognostic information, not evidence that a different treatment helps. Clinical assessment and localisation can establish a disease setting without proving sensitivity to a new drug. A guided intervention then needs evidence for its own strategy and comparator, including recurrence or survival, toxicity, quality of life, anxiety from uncertain results and unnecessary procedures. FDA's nonbinding November 2024 drug-development guidance describes separate proposed uses and asks for randomised trials to evaluate escalation or de-escalation strategies.

Put the action into a complete sentence: for a stated population, using this assay at this time, this qualifying result triggers this action, supported by this strategy evidence. Confirming a low signal, arranging appropriate evaluation, entering a protocol and starting a drug are different actions. A negative result has an action question too: people with favourable outcomes may have received the very treatment someone proposes omitting. Omission safety requires evidence in the matched population and course. Routine follow-up after treatment is a separate clinical plan; an experimental blood-testing schedule does not automatically replace it.

In a fictional proposal, detectable blood after surgery is associated with recurrence, and Drug Q is proposed whenever the signal appears. An observational association has not tested that strategy, even if Drug Q works in another stage or cancer. The proposed study needs the assay rule, any confirmation, disease-extent assessment and safety review before treatment. Finding radiographically detectable disease changes a molecular-only intervention question. A falling blood signal is not automatically a validated substitute for recurrence, survival or quality of life; keep the comparator and adequate follow-up.

A fictional trial randomises assay-positive people to a new strategy or usual care and measures recurrence and harms from the same enrolment point. If its population and methods fit the claim, that comparison tests an action more directly than a series showing that positive tests precede recurrence. Measured lead time is a gap between defined detection events in the study's sampling schedule. Moving the diagnosis clock earlier can lengthen measured survival without delaying death, so extra lead time alone is not benefit. Read the uncertainty, applicability and harms rather than treating a positive signal as proof of a useful intervention.

Colorectal cancer provides evidence for defined residual-disease testing strategies. Postoperative detection carries recurrence hazard ratios of 7 to 18, detection after adjuvant chemotherapy 11 to 51, and serial surveillance up to 43, with recurrence found a mean or median of about 9 to 10 months before imaging and up to 16.5 months (Tie 2016, Reinert 2019, Henriksen 2022). DYNAMIC randomised a defined stage II colon-cancer strategy, cutting adjuvant chemotherapy from 28% to 15% in stage II colon cancer without losing recurrence-free survival (Tie 2022). That strategy does not establish benefit from escalation after a positive result, and about 10% of ctDNA-negative stage II patients still recur.

Detection limits use method-specific quantities, including variant allele fraction, an estimated tumour fraction or tumour-attributed molecules per plasma volume. Converting a concentration into a fraction needs a compatible denominator and the methods' calculation, recovery and calibration; the printed numbers alone are insufficient. A limit also belongs to its specimen, input and calling rule, so product pages using different units do not establish a head-to-head sensitivity ranking.

Detecting pooled tumour-associated signal does not by itself validate naming or measuring a subclone. Subclone assignment needs separate evidence about covered variants, their grouping, the clone model and its detectable abundance under the actual input conditions. Adding targets can improve detection of a tumour signal without establishing detection or quantitation of every individual variant.

strengths: Months of lead time over imaging
limitations: Lead time without proven intervention causes anxiety

records.name: Notch signalling
records.tldr: Notch receptors can relay signals between contacting cells. The effect depends on the receptor, ligand, alteration and tissue; receiving a signal does not by itself prove growth dependence.
records.summary:
A ligand-bearing sender, receptor amount, received signal and growth dependence are separate observations. Locate malignant, vessel and other neighboring cells before assigning a Notch mechanism. Ligand on a vessel is not evidence that the tumor received the signal, and total receptor is different from a released nuclear intracellular domain.

Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

Weng found activating NOTCH1 changes in extracellular heterodimerization or PEST regions in more than half of the studied T-ALLs. Agrawal identified predicted inactivating alterations in head-and-neck squamous tumors, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role there. An uncharacterized allele inherits neither direction from the pathway name; tissue, cell identity and alteration effect matter.

A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.

records.name: AMPK energy sensing
records.tldr: AMPK helps cells adjust their work to their energy supply. Slower growth and better survival can occur together.
records.summary: AMP-activated protein kinase responds to cellular energy state. Structural and biochemical experiments showed that ADP binding protects activating phosphorylation without the direct allosteric activation supplied by AMP. In cancer-model experiments during energy stress, AMPK supported NADPH maintenance through changes in fatty-acid metabolism and prolonged survival. Thus activation cannot be read as a universal cancer-killing signal. Preserve the model, energy conditions, timing, perturbation controls and separate measurements of growth and death. A phosphorylation signal does not establish selective drug action or patient benefit.

records.name: Oxidative phosphorylation
records.tldr: Oxygen use and cellular energy production are related measurements. Researchers need controlled experiments to work out how much energy a cell produces through mitochondrial respiration.
records.summary: Extracellular flux methods estimate respiratory and glycolytic contributions to energy production under defined assumptions. A respiratory message, measured oxygen use, calculated energy output and dependence for survival are distinct claims. Normalisation, fuel, viable-cell input, collection time and the specified method version belong with a result. Electron transport, proton pumping, return through ATP synthase and uncoupling are distinct steps. The mitochondrial matrix and intermembrane space locate the two sides of the inner membrane; naming these compartments does not supply a universal conversion ratio.

In mitochondria, respiratory electron transfer and proton movement are distinct processes. Some respiratory complexes move protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space; return through ATP synthase can support ATP formation, while other return pathways dissipate the gradient without that synthesis step. These directions do not specify a fixed proton-to-ATP ratio. Protons return from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the membrane-embedded Fo part of ATP synthase. A parallel proton leak bypasses ATP synthase and dissipates the gradient. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

records.tldr: Adding phosphate can change a protein’s behavior in several ways. The site and cellular context determine whether a measured change indicates activation, inhibition or something else.
records.summary: Protein kinases commonly transfer phosphate from ATP to a substrate, producing ADP. Protein phosphatases remove phosphate by hydrolysis without regenerating ATP. A modification can affect catalysis, binding, localization or interactions; sites on one protein can have different functions. Src experiments demonstrated an inhibitory tail-phosphorylation mechanism in their defined preparation, so phosphorylation should not be treated as universal activation.

records.name: PI3K / AKT / mTOR
records.tldr: This network links growth signals and nutrients to protein production, metabolism and recycling. Different branches can respond differently to an intervention.
records.summary:
Class I PI3K phosphorylates a membrane lipid, producing PIP3; PTEN removes its position-3 phosphate. AKT and mTOR are protein kinases. A PIP3 lipid result and an AKT1 Ser473 phosphosite result are therefore different molecular measurements. Document specimen preservation, cell mixture, protein site, timing, exposure, comparator and total-protein normalization before interpreting a change as activity or dependence.

Membrane recruitment helps organize AKT activation. PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 Thr308, whereas the rictor-mTOR complex supplies Ser473 phosphorylation in the defined experimental route. AKT can inhibit TSC2, relieving the TSC1/2 brake on RHEB, which promotes mTORC1 signaling. The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.

Raptor-containing mTORC1 and rictor-containing mTORC2 are distinct complexes. mTORC1 regulates protein production and autophagy-initiation machinery; releasing initiation restraint is not proof of completed recycling flux. Harrington linked S6K activity to reduced IRS-1 function, and O'Reilly observed increased IRS-1 and AKT signaling after RAD001 in cell models and treated tumors. Feedback release can change an output without proving that a combination improves outcomes in every setting.

In a fictional mTORC1 perturbation, lower production-regulator phosphorylation followed by higher AKT1 Ser473 and unchanged growth supports biochemical changes, not essentiality or failed engagement; timing alone does not prove the feedback connection. Test the proposed wiring and functional outcome independently. The FDA's 2023 capivasertib-with-fulvestrant approval specified adults with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, qualifying PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations on an approved test and specified prior endocrine treatment or early recurrence. It is not a TNBC indication inferred from a pathway label.

records.tldr: Reactive oxygen species are a group of chemicals with different effects. A fluorescent signal needs its chemistry, location and biological consequence explained.

records.name: Receptor tyrosine kinase activation
records.tldr: Receptor tyrosine kinases can relay signals from outside a cell through protein phosphorylation. Receptor amount, signalling, drug binding and growth dependence are different measurements.
records.summary:
EGFR, FGFR and FLT3 are examples of receptor tyrosine kinases. Their normal roles and activation arrangements differ across receptor families.

Receptor amount, phosphorylation, direct drug engagement, growth dependence and clinical benefit are separate observations. Lower receptor phosphorylation supports a biochemical effect under the assay conditions but can also reflect indirect regulation; it does not by itself prove direct binding. A controlled functional effect with independent specificity tests is needed before assigning receptor dependence.

Many RTKs have extracellular ligand-binding regions, membrane-spanning regions and intracellular tyrosine-kinase machinery. Families activate differently: Zhang demonstrated an asymmetric EGFR kinase-domain interaction, while Stauber examined an FGF1-FGFR2 extracellular complex with a proposed heparin-related assembly arrangement. Ligand, helper molecules, receptor member and context matter. A downstream phosphosite can have multiple upstream causes and is not a universal receptor meter.

Slamon 1987 studied 189 primary breast cancers and reported HER2 amplification in 30%, associated with relapse and survival; that historical study is not a present-day universal prevalence or a causal drug-response experiment. In the 2001 randomized trial of 469 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer, adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy increased median survival from 20.3 to 25.1 months, with cardiac toxicity as a material risk. A trial median summarizes a group and does not predict an individual survival time.

This separates amount, sampled signaling and growth response; the pattern suggests dependence but attribution still needs controls and independent perturbation. RNA is not surface accessibility, a family-name inhibitor need not engage every member at the tested exposure. For an antibody-drug conjugate, receptor access and payload delivery are separate questions from whether growth requires that receptor's signaling. Fixed-tissue staining and viable-model perturbation have different input costs and validation scopes.

records.tldr: Hypoxia is reduced local oxygen availability relative to tissue needs. A response marker or vessel count is not a direct oxygen measurement.
records.summary: Oxygen conditions reflect delivery, diffusion and consumption and can vary across a tumour and over time. HIF-linked responses include oxygen-sensitive protein regulation, but other molecular processes can alter the same readouts. Direct oxygen measurements, protein assays and RNA signatures therefore require different interpretations.

Retain region, time, calibration, handling, cell identity and factors that can alter HIF independently of oxygen; destructive assays use finite material. Thresholds must fit the method and purpose. Vessel density is not flow, HIF abundance is not oxygen concentration, and a specimen average can hide poorly oxygenated regions.

In a fictional biopsy with a high hypoxia-response score, the score alone gives neither an exact oxygen level nor proof that every region is hypoxic. Cell mixture and alternative regulation remain possible explanations, and individual prognosis requires different evidence. Oxygen symbols in a schematic illustrate supply, distance and consumption without measured concentrations or a universal gradient; supply and demand are separate from the response program.

records.name: Tumour-informed versus tumour-naive ctDNA assays
records.tldr: A tumour-informed assay selects features from a sampled tumour for later tracking. A tumour-naive method uses predefined features without first building that patient's tumour reference. Performance and turnaround depend on the actual method and specimen.
records.summary:
A tumour-informed test uses a sampled tumour reference to select features for later tracking in plasma. The reference can come from a suitable biopsy or resection; it is not necessarily a surgically removed whole tumour or a complete inventory of tumour clones. Reference quality, selected targets, plasma input, background and the calling rule affect performance. A fixed list can miss features outside it, including variants that emerge after the reference was sampled.

A tumour-naive or tumour-agnostic method uses predefined features without first building that person's tumour reference. It still needs suitable input and a validated detector, and it does not promise a complete mutation profile. FDA's November 2024 drug-development guidance describes strengths and limits of both approaches rather than a universal ranking. Santonja's same-sample breast-cancer comparison supports its particular assays at low signal, not every branded product. Magbanua's 2025 study also found retained assay variants in sampled resistant tumours from some patients with negative plasma; a negative draw does not by itself prove that the reference targets disappeared.
